# ApplyAudioScene <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Audio](BlitzBasic-Audio)

</div>


```blitzbasic
ApplyAudioScene:Void scene:Int32, fade_ms:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | In | Int32 | required | A scene from [CreateAudioScene](CreateAudioScene). Anything else is a runtime error. |
| `fade_ms` | In | Int32 | `0` | How many milliseconds it takes to get to the values. `0` (the default) sets them at once. Below 0 is a runtime error. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Sets everything that a scene holds, at once or over a fade time. What the scene does not hold is left alone, so scenes can be applied on top of each other. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

## Differences

* A value that is still fading starts from where it is, as with the commands that set it, and they keep working next to scenes.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
ApplyAudioScene paused, 300
```
